interest: This file provides valuable contemporary intelligence on the rapidly warming military and diplomatic relationship between Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan in the wake of the November 1936 Anti-Comintern Pact. It captures striking public and ceremonial gestures—such as armed Japanese sailors parading along Unter den Linden during Skagerrak Day celebrations and the Japanese Embassy being the only foreign mission to fly its colors at half-mast for casualties from the bombed pocket battleship Deutschland. For diplomatic and military historians, the report offers vital early evidence of Axis technical and intelligence cooperation, noting that Japanese naval officers were granted unprecedented access to secret German manufacturing plants under an emerging bilateral intelligence-sharing arrangement.
overview: This file (894.3362/1) from May–June 1937 documents the official visit of the Imperial Japanese Navy heavy cruiser Ashigara to the German ports of Kiel and Berlin following its representation of Japan at the British Coronation Naval Review. The records, comprising an Office of Naval Intelligence attaché report and a State Department cross-reference sheet, highlight the extraordinary diplomatic, ceremonial, and military courtesies extended by Nazi Germany to Japanese naval personnel. German officials arranged a private audience for Japanese officers with Adolf Hitler, high-profile social receptions hosted by Admiral Erich Raeder, and armed Japanese participation in the Skagerrak Day commemoration. Significantly, U.S. naval intelligence observed that Japanese officers were permitted access to restricted German industrial plants not normally shown to foreign military personnel, pointing to the practical implementation of intelligence-sharing agreements under the 1936 Anti-Comintern Pact.

subfiles.about: A U.S. Naval Attaché intelligence report describing the extraordinary official, ceremonial, and industrial courtesies extended by the German government to the officers and crew of the Japanese cruiser Ashigara.
subfiles.summary: This intelligence report details the special privileges and courtesies extended to the officers and crew of the Japanese cruiser Ashigara during their visit to Kiel and Berlin in late May 1937. The officers were granted an unusual private audience with Adolf Hitler, attended opera performances with Admiral Erich Raeder and Nazi leaders, and saw their armed sailors march in the Skagerrak Day parade on Unter den Linden. The report also observes that the Japanese Embassy uniquely flew its flag at half-mast following the bombing of the German pocket battleship Deutschland, and Japanese officers were granted rare access to restricted German industrial facilities, suggesting an active intelligence-exchange agreement under the 1936 Anti-Comintern Pact.
subfiles.title: Naval Attaché's Report on German-Japanese Relations and Courtesies Extended to the Japanese Cruiser Ashigara
subfiles.to: Chief of Naval Operations, Navy Department

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing a prior naval attaché report regarding visits of Japanese naval vessels to German ports.
subfiles.summary: This administrative document file cross-reference sheet records Report No. R-561 (noted as R-361) dated May 27, 1937, from the Naval Attaché. It directs researchers to decimal file 835.3362/1 (or related subject file) regarding the visit of Japanese naval vessels to German ports. The sheet serves as an internal State Department tracking mechanism linking related correspondence on German-Japanese naval contacts.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Report R-561 on Visit of Japanese Naval Vessels to German Ports
